decisions.reason: The quotient charts glue to a closed subscheme of X° × P(W); elimination of a unit coefficient gives P^{r-1}, and r=0 gives the empty scheme. Automorphisms over X° alone need not be trivial. Step 5.1 now requires compatibility with both projections, which forces identity on the quotient charts. The Statement and page claims are unchanged.

The determinant expansion has only its constant and linear epsilon terms, giving 1+epsilon trace(B) in every characteristic. Quotient and localization universal properties give precisely the asserted tangent spaces. At n=1 trace is the identity on k and its kernel is zero; only n>=2 has a nonzero off-diagonal trace-zero matrix. Corrected the contradictory boundary clause without changing the Example.

The title is a descriptive label, not an assertion dropping the explicit perfect-field or rational-point hypotheses. For a finite separable closed residue field the cotangent sequence identifies m/m² with Omega tensor L, whose Jacobian cokernel has dimension n-rank J. Regularity is exactly equality with local dimension. The inseparable nonrational counterexample satisfies neither branch, so it does not refute this item, its contract, or the qualified page description.

Irreducibility of t^p-a requires the specified a not to be a pth power. Imperfection guarantees existence of such an a, not the condition for every a. Corrected the quantifier in 6.1. The field L is regular of dimension zero, whereas its base change L[u]/(u^p) has maximal ideal cotangent dimension one and dimension zero, including p=2. The geometric-regularity supplier applies with the declared AC; no statement change is needed.

The initial ideal is (y²), its degree-one quotient has basis x,y and hence determines the two-dimensional cotangent space and its dual. Only the reduced cone (y=0) spans one line. Corrected the false concluding assertion, the additional false sign-invariance wording, and the nilradical step locator. The explicit Jacobian, initial ideal, monic-division and nilradical computations establish every Example clause without changing it.

Negation scales the derivative row and lowest homogeneous polynomial by -1, so the source qualification was literally false. It preserves the equation ideal, Jacobian kernel, initial ideal and factors up to units. Corrected that clause. Independently, the zero Jacobian gives k², the least degree is two, and y²-x²=(y-x)(y+x) has distinct factors exactly when 2 is nonzero. The Example and its contract remain sound.

The coordinate convention made the displayed h_j undefined at index zero. Explicitly relabelled vector coordinates by 1,...,n to match P, and defined every recursion state, including the skipped s step. Fixed j_m when m=0 and cited regular-local-domain reducedness for the reduction step. The active forms cut dimension by one until their common kernel is kv; the transverse-slice supplier gives a regular smooth local ring at each cut. The zero vector and d=1 branches remain valid, and the Statement is unchanged.

Spec L has one prime and dimension zero, so the rejected boundary assertion was false. Corrected it to distinguish the field cotangent dimension zero from the thickening cotangent dimension one. The s-adic orders in sg^p=f^p differ modulo p, proving s is not a pth power; Frobenius sends every polynomial in alpha into k, proving pure inseparability. The reviewed general theorem then gives the stated regularity and nonsmoothness witness, with no interface change.

The classical charts alone did not supply a scheme to which F39 applies. Added the explicit associated-scheme construction: localized ratio-coordinate maps send g_h to g_i/(x_h)^2, have inverses and satisfy the cocycle condition, so the reduced Spec A_i charts glue. Every prime is now covered. Squarefreeness, pure dimension n-1, nonzero gradient, regular maximal localizations and regular localization justify smoothness over the perfect field and the stated closed-point tangent dimensions. No Example or Statement was changed.

The equality with dim X is a closed-point assertion; the generic point of A¹ has intrinsic tangent dimension zero. Restricted the conclusion of 1.1 to closed points and made the regular-locus existence argument on an explicit reduced affine spectrum. Closed-point density supplies a regular classical point, proving attainment of the lower bound. Automorphism stalk isomorphisms transport regularity, and localization covers nonclosed points without asserting constant intrinsic tangent dimension there. The Statement is unchanged.

Relative transcendence degree r equals dim X-dim Y, so generically finite maps have r=0 and r=1 describes relative dimension one. Corrected that boundary sentence, the Y-point basis claim, the unjustified H=1 assertion and the reversed Frobenius ring-map notation. The main proof is sound: clearing finitely many denominators bounds the relative differential fibre dimension by r, and cotangent transitivity at rational regular points forces differential rank at least dim Y and hence surjectivity. The Statement is unchanged.

A map to Spec k has zero target tangent space, so the zero differential is surjective and remains allowed on V. Corrected the contradictory exclusion, the additional density denial (nonempty opens of irreducible X are dense), and defined the restriction g used in 4.1. Regular affine opens are smooth over k; the tangent criterion applies at every closed point, and the open standard-smooth locus has no nonempty closed complement by closed-point density. This proves all scheme-point assertions without changing the Statement.

The old 4.1 applied the tangent criterion only at classical closed points and did not prove the asserted smoothness at all scheme points. Added the open standard-smooth locus argument: a nonempty closed complement in an affine finite-type chart has a closed point, contradicting the criterion. Restricted tangent and fibre computations explicitly to closed points; closed-point density preserves component dimensions, and base change gives fibre smoothness over k because k(y)=k. The critical-locus bound has smooth source and target and yields a proper image closure. Statement unchanged.

The kernel theorem requires generation of the actual ideal, not retention of every entry of an original list. For (x,x), the proper sublist (x) qualifies. Corrected the paragraph to distinguish generating and nongenerating sublists. The intrinsic tangent, full graded cone, regular-versus-smooth and smooth-source conventions agree with the inspected supplier interfaces and page; its contract imposes no contrary generating-list requirement. No Statement or Definition section changes.

F3 explicitly cites step 2.1 of the incidence proof, which actually constructs I_X as a closed subscheme of X × P^r and restricts it to X°. The checked quotient charts and unit transition equations prove this embedding; thus it supplies more than the asserted locally closed immersion. Its use for separatedness is mathematically licensed, although the contract quotation reproduces only the Statement. Regularity makes the finite incidence components disjoint open integral schemes; separatedness permits the classical dictionary, and target generic smoothness on each component gives the common nonempty parameter open and smooth whole fibres. No repair is necessary.

At a nonclosed t the combined fibre Jacobian computes Omega over kappa(t), so the old absolute-k claim was false. Repaired 2.3/3.2 by constructing the defect and emptiness loci entirely on classical pairs, where kappa(x)=kappa(t)=k. The intrinsic cotangent dimension makes the polynomial-minor loci agree on overlaps; classical projective projection is closed, and the parameter dictionary transfers its complement to a scheme open. Later steps explicitly fix closed t, then prove regularity at every point of its fibre by openness and closed-point density. Bertini and componentwise dimension drop produce a good tuple, and a form avoiding the finite zero-dimensional intersection proves r>d. Also bounded induction by the available degrees and corrected local-spectrum wording. Statement unchanged.
